newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arrest warrant issued for former East German leader.
newsitem.headline: Arrest warrant issued for former East German leader.

text.p: Justice authorities in Berlin on Thursday issued arrest warrants for East Germany's last hardline communist leader, Egon Krenz, and three of his top deputies, a Berlin court spokesman said.

The move followed a decision on Tuesday by the supreme court which ruled that former East German leaders could be sent to jail for having ordered border guards to "shoot to kill" people who tried to flee across the Berlin Wall in the Cold War years.
Krenz and the three others who are facing manslaughter charges in a separate trial were served with the arrest warrants at the start of a court session in Berlin on Thursday.
Justice ministry spokesman Ruediger Reiff linked the move to the supreme court ruling but said Krenz and three leaders from the defunct communist state would not be jailed.
But he said they would have to surrender their passports and and may not leave Berlin or Brandenburg state.
The supreme court ruling meant that it did not agree with claims by Krenz and other former communist officials that united Germany practised "victors' justice" against them.
